scope: Ghost admission and resurrection with a corpse in another instance of the same map

finding.before: MapManager validates corpse map ancestry, but InstanceMap::CanEnter did not validate the actual selected copy. HandleWorldPortAck used the global corpse cache and checked only mapId. A permitted transfer into B resurrected a ghost and deleted its corpse in A.
finding.reference: Native map1648 instance1 corpse; native group selection instance2; ordinary preflight admitted1; actual GM transfer and ACK returned instance2 alive1 corpse0. Logged in .codex/ghost-instance-reference-native.log.
finding.fix: After the existing GM admission bypass, InstanceMap::CanEnter rejects a dead Player whose same-map corpse has another instanceId, using existing TRANSFER_ABORT_LOCKED_TO_DIFFERENT_INSTANCE. ACK independently requires matching mapId and instanceId before resurrection/corpse conversion, including GM transfers.
finding.data: No SQL migration, map whitelist, forced corpse routing, bind reset or personal-character repair.

native_checks: 24 different-instance cases across LFR17, Normal14, Heroic15, Mythic16 and Human/Orc; each runs in an ordinary death/repop return or one of16 real logout/deleted-Player component reloads.

A is the actually earned Trial of Valor instance with Odyn/Guarm DONE and encounter mask3. B is a distinct instance created by native CreateMap for a separate native group, at the same map/difficulty. The corpse is never moved or rewritten to manufacture a mismatch.

The subject group is temporarily unbound/rebound through native APIs to select B. Ordinary CanPlayerEnter and SafeTeleport are rejected while corpse/ghost/exterior state remain intact. Living and unreleased dead/no-corpse inputs still pass direct InstanceMap admission into empty B.

The existing GM bypass permits actual SafeTeleport and WorldPortAck into B, so ACK is tested independently of the new ordinary admission guard. Ghost/death/health, original corpse GUID/instance and its SQL row survive; repeated ACK is inert.

The native fixture restores group A, returns to the exterior through real transfer/ACK, clears GM, checks another denied ordinary transfer to B, then restores A. Native script SaveToDB persists the earned checkpoint; exactly one original group_instance row remains, personal bind pointer/permanence stay unchanged, A mask3 and B mask0 survive.

All24 cases then use actual entrance720 and native5775, returning normally to A with50% resurrection, one corpse conversion, repeat-ACK safety and correct SQL save. All72 graveyard/logout cases and16 prepared ghost login component cases pass; final Server/DBErrors logs have no errors.

Canonical Release disassembly is exception-bounded and resolves incremental thunks. Compiled ABI evidence identifies WorldObject instance offset952/0x3B8 and Map instance offset1788/0x6FC. The deployed admission compares these and sends locked-instance12h on mismatch; deployed ACK compares player/corpse instance IDs and jumps past resurrection on mismatch. Prior preflight, portal ghost/living gates and successful resurrection calls remain verified.
Test-CorpseRestartNative.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary passes against the rebuilt canonical executable and actual final-link library, retaining the previous independent-process saved corpse identity fix.
Test-ScenarioResume.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary and Test-ScepterLogin.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary pass. These are native/component and PE checks, not authenticated client login.

Release worldserver and bnetserver built in build-extractors/bin/Release using original generated final-link libraries, without OutDir override. Hidden validation-owned worldserver PID32240 reached ready and exited gracefully0; startup DBErrors/stderr are empty. No servers left running.
retained_failures: .codex/ghost-instance-reference.log initially failed fixture compilation by calling private MapInstanced::CreateInstance. The corrected fixture uses public CreateMap with a real separate-group selector.

.codex/ghost-instance-reference-native.log reproduces the real pre-fix corpse loss. Pre-fix game.lib is retained in build-extractors/runtime-test/ghost-instance-reference with commit.txt and game.sha256.
.codex/ghost-instance-fixed.log passed all native cases before adding ABI, repeated-ACK and persisted-checkpoint assertions. It is intermediate evidence only.

.codex/ghost-instance-final.log correctly rejected the expanded LFR checkpoint assertion. Native LFR BindToInstance does not persist a checkpoint by itself; the fixture had explicitly unbound its previous SQL row. The final fixture invokes the existing InstanceScript::SaveToDB on already earned state after restoring A. No boss state/mask is assigned and no production persistence behavior is changed.
limits: Native socketless synchronous fixtures freeze actor scheduling and use disposable schema-only character/auth data. Group binding changes use native UnbindInstance/BindToInstance; actual invitation/leave/join packets are not exercised.

The foreign-instance real ACK is deliberately exercised through the existing GM admission bypass. Ordinary loaded-target admission and SafeTeleport are tested as rejected; a non-GM foreign-instance AddPlayer is not claimed.

The16 relog cases restore saved fields and native prepared group/bind/aura/LoadCorpse components after actual Player deletion. They do not execute aggregate Player::LoadFromDB or authenticate a client. Independent cold-process testing covers corpse persistence separately, not a full cold raid/group/Player reconstruction.

Corpse-map ancestry remains unchanged and the new selected-copy guard applies only when corpseMapId matches that map. Nested-parent traversal is inspected in source, not newly exercised in a nested dungeon fixture. Living and no-corpse admission behavior are preserved, not redesigned.

An unloaded selected map can still pass map-level preflight before the actual InstanceMap admission at ACK; that existing fallback/homebind path and admission/bind races between request and ACK remain separate cases. No automatic routing into a corpse instance overrides valid group/raid bindings.

Client error text, ghost movement/visibility, loading, corpse/bones visuals, full server-restart network relog, camera/pet/UI and retail traversal/timing still require client verification. No exact retail packet evidence is claimed.

source_evidence.native: ObjectAccessor::AddCorpsesToGrid already scopes a corpse to its instance; Corpse::SaveToDB persists instanceId. The global cache lookup in ACK previously bypassed that distinction.
source_evidence.qualification: Sibling emulator source confirms corpse-map ancestry is a distinct preflight concern. Its current corpse/map architecture is different; it is comparison material, not proof of Legion retail packet behavior.
